VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The counterexample uses E=(0,1), which is nonempty, bounded, and open. The function f(x)=x is continuous and bounded. The supremum 1 and infimum 0 exist but are not attained; for any p∈E there exists p′∈E with f(p′)>f(p), so no greatest value exists. Empty and degenerate cases are avoided (E is nondegenerate). The refutation holds at both endpoints.
